display: I run a small gallery in Alfama, Lisbon, devoted to indigenous textiles. Every maker is named on the wall label. Our current show is Quechua belts from Chinchero.

signals.text: I have an open slot in the May 2027 design week and no show to put in it yet.
I am looking for an exhibition idea that has a real reason to exist, not one that just fills the gap. A textile tradition or community with a story that has not been shown in Lisbon would suit.
The design-week committee needs my programme concept by 15 December.
My shortlist of candidates is thin. I would like to meet a weaving community I do not yet know well, such as Hmong story cloth makers, or hear who else is out there.
A visa problem stopped an Andean weaving collective from coming. I would like to hear how others get artisans, or at least their work, across borders.
I am fighting my printer over label typefaces. He keeps shrinking the makers' names to enlarge the title, and I want the names to stay legible.
Scaffolding has blocked the gallery entrance for eleven months, and the end date keeps slipping. I would like ways to keep visitors coming.
The catalogue for the gallery's tenth year is laid out but unwritten. I need a push, an editor, or a writing partner for the essays.
I would like to bring one of the weavers named on my walls to Lisbon to see her work on them.
I need a good week of mounting help and foot traffic for the Quechua belts opening on 17 October.
I feel the pressure of an empty slot, both for my standing with the committee and for the cost of keeping the space running.
A curator from the textile museum in Porto and I are having lunch on 24 October. I would like to turn it into a collaboration.

offers.text: A 70 m² ground-floor gallery in Alfama with north light and a small storage room, available for exhibitions and talks.
Twenty years of relationships with weaving cooperatives in Peru, Guatemala, Norway (Sami) and Mindanao. I can make introductions where the group agrees.
A mailing list of about 1,400 collectors, curators and interior designers in textiles and design.
Conservation basics: mounting, humidity control and safe hanging for fragile textiles.
A maker-named labelling practice: wall text and press material that credit each weaver by name, village, year and dye plant. I can share how I do it.
A standing exhibitor invitation at Lisbon design week, and a working relationship with its committee.
Fluent Portuguese, English and Spanish, and working French, for translation and for talking with cooperatives and collectors.
Experience organising shipping, customs and insurance for fragile textiles arriving from Latin America.
An assistant who runs Instagram and shipping and can help on a small collaborative show.
A contact in Berlin's sound design scene, who could be an intro for a project that needs sound or an installation.

catchers.hypo: I'm a curator and I'm putting together a show on a textile tradition that has never been shown in Portugal. I need a venue, and a gallery that credits the makers by name.
catchers.can: I can offer the Alfama space for the May 2027 design-week slot, if the project is serious and names its makers. I can also work on the concept with the curator before the committee's deadline.
catchers.confirm: Does the show present the makers by name, with a community that agrees to be shown and with provenance you can document?

catchers.hypo: I work with a weaving or embroidery community outside the usual circuit, such as Hmong, Kuna, or Central Asian. We want to show work in Europe but have no gallery.
catchers.can: I can look at their work and talk about a show in Lisbon. I can advise on mounting, shipping and insurance, and on how the labels should read.
catchers.confirm: Are the weavers willing to be named individually, and can you document where and by whom each piece was made?

catchers.hypo: I'm an anthropologist or an NGO worker supporting a group of women weavers. We have a visa and travel problem for an exhibition abroad.
catchers.can: I know what happened with the Andean collective, and I can share that experience and what I would do differently. I can also join an effort to get the weavers to Lisbon.
catchers.confirm: Is the problem a visa or travel barrier for the weavers themselves, and not a shipping problem?

catchers.hypo: I'm a writer or editor. I read about your gallery's tenth year and would like to help you finish a catalogue of essays and photographs.
catchers.can: I have a designed layout and the material for the book. I need an editor or co-writer for the essays, and I can pay for that.
catchers.confirm: Are you comfortable with a book where each maker is named, and with working to the gallery's voice rather than imposing your own?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young founder of a small craft or design shop in Lisbon. I'm struggling with Instagram, shipping and wholesale, and I'd like a conversation with someone who has done it.
catchers.can: I can talk it through myself, and my assistant Inês knows the practical parts of Instagram and shipping and can help a small shop with its setup.
catchers.confirm: Is your work in handmade or indigenous craft, with the makers named?

catchers.hypo: I'm a sound artist or musician in Berlin. I'd like to build an installation for a textile exhibition.
catchers.can: I can introduce you to someone in Berlin's sound design scene, and I can host a sound-and-textile piece in Alfama.
catchers.confirm: Would the sound piece sit alongside the textiles and respect the makers' work, without taking it over?

catchers.hypo: I'm a collector or interior designer. I'm looking for a textile with a real story, and I want to know who made it.
catchers.can: I can show you work with full maker credits and talk through provenance and display.
catchers.confirm: Do you want pieces credited by maker and village, and not sold as anonymous folk art?

catchers.hypo: I'm a museum curator. We are looking for partners for a touring exhibition of indigenous textiles.
catchers.can: I can co-develop the show, offer my cooperative relationships, and lend the Alfama space as a stop.
catchers.confirm: Does the exhibition name each weaver and have the community's consent?

forbids.text: I do not show or sell work without naming the maker. No anonymous "folk art" and no generic "Peruvian" labels.
I will not work with sellers who cannot show provenance.
I will not ship fragile pieces without proper mounting or insurance.
I cannot spend more than about 12,000 euros on the May show, which covers freight and mounting.
I will not fill the slot with a show that has no reason to exist.

projects.name: Design-week programme 2027
projects.text: An exhibition for the Alfama gallery's May 2027 design-week slot. It needs a concept with a reason to exist, makers who agree to be named, freight and insurance, and a name for the committee by 15 December.

projects.name: Catalogue for the gallery's tenth year
projects.text: A small book with essays and photographs. The layout is done and the text is not.

policy.t1: The open May 2027 design-week slot, the approximate budget, the 15 December deadline, my contacts with cooperatives and my collaborator network.
policy.t2: How the empty slot weighs on my standing with the committee and on the gallery's running costs.
policy.never: My family matters, my health, and the gallery's accounts.
